newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine 91-day bill sale forecast at 6.50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Argentine 91-day bill sale forecast at 6.50 pct.

text.p: Argentine bond market players forecast a cut-off discount rate of 6.50 percent for the 250 million peso sale of 91-day Letes bills Tuesday.
That rate would be somewhat higher than the 6.40 percent cut-off seen at the last Letes auction of similar maturity in January.
A Reuters poll on 91-day peso bills found most players expected a rate of 6.50 percent, with a range from 6.40 percent to 6.50 percent.
"I think there will be strong demand for the peso bills from local and foreign investors," said a trader.
For the $250 million 182-day bills also being auctioned Tuesday, most market watchers expect a discount rate around 6.50 percent. Forecasts ranged from 6.40 to 6.75 percent.
Argentina's last sale of dollar-denominated 182-day bills on November 12 drew a discount rate of 6.80 percent.
In peso terms, bills of that same maturity auctioned last month drew a 6.90 percent rate.
Tuesday's auction will be Argentina's second bill auction of the year. The sale will be done by Dutch auction-style. The debt will settle February 14.
Offers are due by 1400 local time/1700 GMT.
